linux.fallback: Java archives only; machine roots only (per-user installs are not read); any budget, unreadable directory or unenumerable archive answers constrained
linux.mechanism: bounded read-only walk of /opt, /usr/share/java, /usr/lib/jvm, /usr/local/lib, /usr/local/share and /usr/share/maven; no link followed at any path component; archive central directory, pom.properties and MANIFEST.MF read in-process; network mounts skipped via /proc/<pid>/mountinfo

macos.fallback: Java archives only; machine roots only (per-user installs are not read); any budget, unreadable directory or unenumerable archive answers constrained
macos.mechanism: bounded read-only walk of /Applications, /Library/Java, /usr/local and /opt/homebrew; no link followed at any path component; archive central directory, pom.properties and MANIFEST.MF read in-process; network mounts skipped via getmntinfo_r_np

windows.fallback: not read yet: one unsupported status row, windows:planned
windows.mechanism: bounded Program Files walk with the same archive reads

caveats: **Java archives only, machine roots only.** Python and Node components are not read, and the six roots on Linux and four on macOS are fixed: an archive in a per-user location, a home directory or a custom prefix is not looked for.
**No Windows leg yet.** Windows answers one `unsupported` status row (`windows:planned`); a Program Files walk with the same archive reads follows as a later change.

**Completeness is bounded, not guaranteed.** A scan that reaches a bound answers `constrained` and returns what it reached; one blocked read inside a directory listing or file read is not interrupted by the 45 second budget. The 400,000-entry budget is shared by every root, so the roots are walked cheapest first (on macOS `/Applications`, whose app bundles hold many entries, is last): a host whose first roots exhaust it answers `constrained` with `budget_entries` and the later roots are not walked. The network-mount guard is a snapshot of a deny-list: a mount that appears after the table was read, a stacked filesystem over a dead mount or a network filesystem type not on the list is not seen.

**Names are parsed, not proven; nested libraries are listed, not read.** Only `BOOT-INF/lib/`, `WEB-INF/lib/` and `lib/` entries ending `.jar` are listed, from the central directory; their version comes from the entry name alone, so a nested library with an unversioned name reads `unreadable`, and a qualifier word the parser does not know reads as a classifier (nested `guava-31.1-jre.jar` reads `31.1`). An outer archive with no `pom.properties` or manifest takes the file name's word too. A pre-release or build qualifier (`alpha`, `beta`, `rc`, `m`, `ea`, `preview`, `snapshot`, digits and dots) stays in the version. An OSGi-style name (`name_1.2.3...`) keeps everything after the `_` as its version, a classifier word included (`bundle_1.2.3-sources.jar` reads `1.2.3-sources`). Separately, a sole `pom.properties` is trusted: an archive that has no pom of its own but bundles exactly one dependency's reads that dependency's version, marked `pom`, when its file name has no version (`app.jar`, `ROOT.war`); a name that carries a version keeps it (`myapp-2.0.jar` is not affected) unless the archive's value sits in the name; with two or more poms the name rule applies.

**Not collected yet; one kill switch, no customer opt-out.** The daily report does not carry these rows. The per-plugin kill switch exists (`component_inventory/scan`, `PUT /api/v1/plugin-config/component_inventory/kill-switch`), but the permanent customer opt-out of ADR-0028 Decisions 2 and 8 is still open (#7737).

definitions.description: Reports Java archives (.jar, .war, .ear) and the libraries nested one level inside them, found under the machine-wide application roots: one row per archive and per nested library (name, version and where the version came from, path, size, modification time and the application folder it sits under). Linux and macOS only; per-user locations are not read and Windows is not read yet. No process is started and no nested archive is unpacked. A `supported` status means the scan finished and read everything it opened in full, naming in a token any link or network mount it passed over; a `constrained` status means a bound was hit or something could not be read in full, so the list may be incomplete, and it names its one cause. When time runs out, archives not yet read give no rows, and a walk that used the whole budget returns none. Use it for software no package manager owns; for packaged applications use crossplatform.software.inventory and for installed Java runtimes crossplatform.runtimes.jvm. `supported` with no component rows means none was found at the roots, not that none is installed. The result is a live read made when the instruction runs, not a stored snapshot, at a cost of up to 45 seconds and 400,000 directory entries, and it cannot be cancelled once started. Terminal causes (a repeat gives the same answer): budget_entries, section_rows, anchor_rows, depth, dir_truncated, archive_unenumerated. Retryable causes: budget_time, dir_unreadable, archive_changed, mount_table_unreadable, internal_error. The version comes from the file name; the archive corrects it only when the name carries the archive's version.

description: Installed software components found in application trees (Java archives)
how_it_works:
`scan` answers one question: which Java archives, and which libraries bundled inside them, sit in the machine-wide application trees of this host. It takes no parameters; the roots come from the OS leg and from nothing a request can supply.

The leg reads the mount table once, drops any root that is missing, reached through a link or on a network mount, and walks the rest breadth first without following a link at any path component: a link met inside a tree is not entered, and a `supported` status row says so with `link_skipped`. Every file ending `.jar`, `.war` or `.ear` is opened once and read in-process: the archive's central directory is parsed and the libraries nested one level deep (`BOOT-INF/lib/`, `WEB-INF/lib/`, `lib/`) are listed from that directory alone. The network types come from the shared list in `agents/shared/network_fstype.hpp`, which also names `ncpfs`, `coda`, `smb2` and the network-backed FUSE clients `gcsfuse`, `goofys`, `blobfuse`, `blobfuse2`, `ossfs`, `obsfs`, `cosfs`, `juicefs`, `mfsmount`, `moosefs`, `lizardfs`, `seaweedfs`, `weed`, `curlftpfs`, `httpfs2`, `s3ql`, `onedrive`, `google-drive-ocamlfuse`, `davfs2` and `fuse-nfs` (a mount of those types is treated as a network mount); an unlisted FUSE subtype and a stacked filesystem over a network mount are not detected by this list.

The version comes from the file name. The scan asks the archive (`pom.properties`, then `MANIFEST.MF`) only when the name gave none or is ambiguous, and an archive value replaces the file name's split only when the file name carries it (`<name>-<version>` or `<name>-<version>-...`; `<name>_<version>` for an OSGi `Bundle-Version`). A `pom.properties` is used only when it is the archive's only one or the only one whose artifact segment (`META-INF/maven/<group>/<artifact>/`) equals the archive's name, because a shaded archive carries its dependencies' own; otherwise the manifest decides, else the version is `unreadable`.

No nested archive is unpacked, no `java` process is started and nothing is written to the host except the plugin's own cost counters. The plugin is not a vulnerability matcher, not a package-manager query and not a view of per-user installs.

### What you can decide with it

| Question | Linux | macOS |
|---|---|---|
| Which Java archives are installed under the application trees, at what version? | One row per `.jar`, `.war` or `.ear` under `/opt`, `/usr/share/java`, `/usr/lib/jvm`, `/usr/local/lib`, `/usr/local/share` and `/usr/share/maven` | One row per archive under `/Applications`, `/Library/Java`, `/usr/local` and `/opt/homebrew` |
| Which libraries ride inside an application archive? | One row per nested library, with the path `<archive>!<entry>` and the application folder it belongs to | The same |
| Can this list be trusted as complete? | Yes only when the status is `supported` and no token names something passed over (`root_link_skipped`, `link_skipped`, `network_fs_skipped`), which a `supported` answer carries; `constrained` names its one cause | The same |

What a result proves. `supported` means the scan finished: no bound was reached and every directory and archive it opened was read in full. What it passed over on purpose (a link, a network mount) is named by an informational token on the status row, never silent. It does not mean nothing is installed outside the roots above, or in a per-user location. `constrained` means a bound was reached or something could not be read in full, so the list may be incomplete; the rows already read are still returned, but when time runs out archives not yet read give no rows, and a walk that used the whole budget returns none. A row whose version no source gives is listed with `version_source` `unreadable`; that is a gap in one row and does not make the scan constrained.
name: component_inventory

columns.description: Row shape discriminator (the wire row's leading tag). Values: status (exactly one per result, always first), comp (one per archive or nested library found).
columns.name: row_kind

columns.description: Component kind. Values: java. Status rows: the action name (scan).
columns.name: kind

columns.description: Artifact name taken from the file name, without the version and extension (log4j-core-2.17.1.jar reads log4j-core). A name with bytes outside printable ASCII is kept with those bytes shown as ?; pipes, backslashes and line breaks are escaped or flattened on the wire. Status rows: the level (supported, constrained or unsupported).
columns.name: name

columns.description: Version from the file name, corrected by the archive's pom.properties or MANIFEST.MF only when the file name carries that version; when the name gives none, from pom.properties, else MANIFEST.MF; empty when none gives one. Nested libraries take it from the entry name only. A pre-release or build qualifier (rc, beta, M1, snapshot, a build number) stays in it. Status rows: the comma-joined cause tokens, or -.
columns.name: version

columns.description: Where the version came from. Values: filename, pom, manifest, unreadable (no source gave a version; the row is still listed and the scan is not made incomplete by it).
columns.name: version_source

columns.description: Absolute path of the archive; a nested library is <archive path>!<entry name>. A NUL or a byte outside valid UTF-8 in a folder, file or entry name is shown as ?.
columns.name: path

columns.description: Size in bytes: the archive file size, or the nested entry's uncompressed size.
columns.name: size

columns.description: Modification time of the archive file as Unix seconds; a nested library carries its archive's.
columns.name: mtime

columns.description: First path component below the scanned root: the application folder the archive sits under (the file name itself when it sits directly in a root). A NUL or a byte outside valid UTF-8 in the name is shown as ?.
columns.name: anchor_app

outputs_note: Every row is pipe-delimited. The first row is always `status|scan|<level>|<tokens>` (`level` is `supported`, `constrained` or `unsupported`; `tokens` is comma-joined cause tokens, or `-`). Component rows follow as `comp|java|<name>|<version>|<version_source>|<path>|<size>|<mtime>|<anchor_app>`, one per archive and one per nested library; the first field is `row_kind` (`status` or `comp`) and is the first column below, and on a status row the next columns carry the action name, the level and the tokens. `version` is empty when `version_source` is `unreadable`. `supported` with zero component rows and no informational token means none was found at the roots; `constrained` means the list may be incomplete. Rows are written at both levels.

privileges.runs_as: n/a: the leg is planned and reads nothing

privileges.grant: None expected: application trees under `/Applications`, `/Library/Java`, `/usr/local` and `/opt/homebrew` are normally world-readable (inferred, not measured as the agent account); the mount table read (`getmntinfo_r_np`) needs no grant
privileges.if_refused: A directory that cannot be listed records `macos:component_inventory:dir_unreadable` and the answer is `constrained`; an archive that cannot be read in full records `macos:component_inventory:archive_unenumerated`
privileges.measured: See the sample below if one is present for this leg; otherwise not measured
privileges.runs_as: agent daemon (root under the shipped LaunchDaemon today, `docs/agent-privilege-model.md`)

privileges.grant: None expected: the roots under `/opt` and `/usr` are normally world-readable (inferred, not measured as the packaged account); `/proc/<pid>/mountinfo` (the agent's own pid) is world-readable; the packaged unit also holds ambient `CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH`, which makes `dir_unreadable` rarely reachable there
privileges.if_refused: A directory that cannot be listed records `linux:component_inventory:dir_unreadable` and the answer is `constrained`; an unreadable mount table walks nothing and records `linux:component_inventory:mount_table_unreadable`
privileges.measured: See the sample below if one is present for this leg; otherwise not measured
privileges.runs_as: agent daemon, dedicated unprivileged account (`yuzu-agent` on the packaged unit), never root by design (`docs/agent-privilege-model.md`)

result_status.when: The scan finished with no bound reached and every directory and archive it opened read in full, populated or empty. Informational tokens may still ride the status row without changing the level: `<os>:component_inventory:root_link_skipped` (a root was dropped for a link), `<os>:component_inventory:link_skipped` (a link inside a tree was not entered or listed; no link is followed), `<os>:component_inventory:network_fs_skipped` (a root or a directory inside the tree sat on a network mount and was passed over) and `<os>:component_inventory:version_unreadable` (at least one row has no version)

A bound was reached (`budget_entries`, `budget_time`, `section_rows`, `anchor_rows`, `depth`), a directory could not be listed (`dir_unreadable`) or was cut at its entry cap (`dir_truncated`), an archive could not be enumerated (`archive_unenumerated`: it could not be opened or read, is not a ZIP archive or is cut short, uses ZIP64, has a directory over 16 MiB, an entry name over 1,024 bytes, an encrypted entry or a corrupt record) or changed while it was read (`archive_changed`), or the mount table could not be read so nothing was walked (`mount_table_unreadable`). `os` is `linux` or `macos`. The first cause recorded is the one reported. `internal_error` (`linux:component_inventory:internal_error`, `macos:component_inventory:internal_error`, `windows:component_inventory:internal_error`) is the catch-all for an unexpected failure and the command fails

Only the Windows leg is declared planned today (the other two tokens are the shared reporter's and are not emitted by a shipped leg): the action answers `status|scan|unsupported|windows:planned` and nothing else

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result.** Every row is server instruction-result data, with the standard retention policy, served over REST `/api/responses`. Nothing here is a durable server-side table of its own.

**Not consumed by** the daily sync, Echo, DEX or metrics: the action runs on demand only. The plugin publishes the cost of its last scan as the agent's `yuzu.plugin.component_inventory.*` heartbeat tags (entries walked, rows, milliseconds, roots skipped, links skipped, mounts skipped).

**Sensitivity.** Rows name the archives and libraries installed on the device, with their versions, paths and application folder names, which is a detailed software inventory for that device. The root list holds only machine-wide locations and no per-user location is in it; that is a property of the list, not a boundary the scan enforces, so an archive found under a root is read wherever it sits. Names are echoed as they appear on disk (scrubbed for the wire only), and the names of nested libraries can reveal a customer's internal dependency names.
